pr.title: Add Client resource type and its scopes to authorization schema and e…

raw_findings.body: The existing resource server is returned unchanged by init(), so it lacks the Clients all-resource and the newly introduced scopes. Creating an individual client resource attempts to attach every Clients scope and fails when a new scope is absent, making client permissions unusable after upgrade.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Existing persisted V2 authorization data is incompatible with the newly required client scopes and resources.
raw_findings.impact: The existing resource server is returned unchanged by init(), so it lacks the Clients all-resource and the newly introduced scopes. Creating an individual client resource attempts to attach every Clients scope and fails when a new scope is absent, making client permissions unusable after upgrade.
raw_findings.root_cause: The schema map was expanded without migrating resource servers that were already initialized from the previous schema.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an upgrade/backfill path for an existing admin-permissions client that creates missing schema scopes and missing all-resource resources (including Clients) instead of returning without reconciliation.
raw_findings.title: Backfill the Clients schema for existing admin-permissions realms
raw_findings.trigger: A realm has V2 admin permissions enabled and an admin-permissions client created by a version that only had the Users resource type, then the server is upgraded and an administrator creates a permission for an individual client.

raw_findings.body: The lookup does not find the resource created by AdminPermissionsSchema, which records the owner as resourceServer.getClientId(). Evaluation falls back to the all-clients resource and denies the otherwise valid per-client permission.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Per-client grants are treated as absent and protected client operations return Forbidden.
raw_findings.impact: The lookup does not find the resource created by AdminPermissionsSchema, which records the owner as resourceServer.getClientId(). Evaluation falls back to the all-clients resource and denies the otherwise valid per-client permission.
raw_findings.root_cause: The lookup uses the resource-server identifier as a resource owner although schema-created resources are owned by the resource-server client.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass server.getClientId() as the owner ID, or use the owner-independent findByName overload as the user V2 evaluator does.
raw_findings.title: Use the resource-server client ID when looking up individual client resources
raw_findings.trigger: A same-realm administrator is granted a scope permission for one client and then accesses that client while the resource server ID differs from its client ID.

raw_findings.body: The owner-constrained lookup returns null even though the all-clients resource exists, so every global client-scope permission evaluates to false.
raw_findings.failure_mode: All-clients permissions fail to authorize requests.
raw_findings.impact: The owner-constrained lookup returns null even though the all-clients resource exists, so every global client-scope permission evaluates to false.
raw_findings.root_cause: The global-resource lookup uses resourceServer.getId() instead of the owner used for admin-permissions resources.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use server.getClientId() for the owner constraint or the two-argument findByName overload used by getResourceTypeResource().
raw_findings.title: Look up the all-clients resource with its actual owner
raw_findings.trigger: A same-realm administrator has an all-clients VIEW or MANAGE permission and the resource server ID differs from the resource-server client ID.

raw_findings.body: The method omits those resources because getOrCreateResource creates object resources and assigns scopes but does not assign their resource type; only the all-clients resource is initialized with type Clients. Callers receive an empty or incomplete set of client IDs despite valid per-client grants.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The permission-discovery API cannot report individual client permissions correctly.
raw_findings.impact: The method omits those resources because getOrCreateResource creates object resources and assigns scopes but does not assign their resource type; only the all-clients resource is initialized with type Clients. Callers receive an empty or incomplete set of client IDs despite valid per-client grants.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new type-based enumeration assumes individual schema resources carry a type that the schema creation path does not populate.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set resource.setType(resourceType) when schema object resources are created, and retain the type-based query (or query the resources through the associated permissions instead).
raw_findings.title: Ensure per-client schema resources have the Clients type before filtering them
raw_findings.trigger: A caller invokes getClientsWithPermission after permissions have created individual client resources through AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource.

raw_findings.body: The administrator can manage client scopes because canManageClientScopes checks MANAGE, and can view individual client scopes because canView(ClientScopeModel) checks MANAGE, but is denied the collection-level view operation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A principal receives Forbidden for client-scope listing despite holding the stronger management permission.
raw_findings.impact: The administrator can manage client scopes because canManageClientScopes checks MANAGE, and can view individual client scopes because canView(ClientScopeModel) checks MANAGE, but is denied the collection-level view operation.
raw_findings.root_cause: The V2 global view predicate does not preserve the manage-implies-view relationship used by the client-scope permission methods.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Include hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) in canView(), or override canViewClientScopes() to allow the all-clients MANAGE grant.
raw_findings.title: Treat an all-clients MANAGE grant as permission to view client scopes
raw_findings.trigger: An administrator has only the V2 all-clients MANAGE permission and calls an endpoint guarded by requireViewClientScopes(), such as listing realm client scopes.

raw_findings.body: The outer condition passes, but management() selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever V2 is enabled. The event handler then calls a V2 setPermissionsEnabled method, which throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing removal-event processing to fail.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Provider event processing aborts with UnsupportedOperationException in a valid combined-feature configuration.
raw_findings.impact: The outer condition passes, but management() selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever V2 is enabled. The event handler then calls a V2 setPermissionsEnabled method, which throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing removal-event processing to fail.
raw_findings.root_cause: The listener is gated by V1 alone even though evaluator selection gives V2 precedence.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Only run this legacy cleanup branch when V1 is enabled and V2 is disabled, or implement a V2-specific removal cleanup path that does not invoke unsupported legacy methods.
raw_findings.title: Do not dispatch removal cleanup to V2 evaluators when both feature versions are enabled
raw_findings.trigger: Both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 are enabled and a role, client, or group removal event is emitted.

raw_findings.body: The new guard skips the ClientRemovedEvent branch entirely. The target client is deleted, but its resource and policies remain in the admin-permissions resource server as orphaned authorization data.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Deleted clients leave stale permission resources and policies in persistent authorization storage.
raw_findings.impact: The new guard skips the ClientRemovedEvent branch entirely. The target client is deleted, but its resource and policies remain in the admin-permissions resource server as orphaned authorization data.
raw_findings.root_cause: The V1-only feature guard suppresses all removal handling under the normal V2-only configuration.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add V2-specific cleanup for ClientRemovedEvent that deletes the schema resource and its associated permissions, while keeping the legacy setPermissionsEnabled cleanup confined to V1.
raw_findings.title: Remove V2 client authorization resources when their client is deleted
raw_findings.trigger: Only V2 is enabled, a client has one or more per-client V2 permission resources, and that client is deleted.

raw_findings.body: The documentation says the method "Returns true" even though it is void and, like the other require methods, throws ForbiddenException when authorization fails.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The public evaluator API documents behavior that the method cannot provide.
raw_findings.impact: The documentation says the method "Returns true" even though it is void and, like the other require methods, throws ForbiddenException when authorization fails.
raw_findings.root_cause: The method received a boolean-predicate documentation template instead of a require-method contract.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the return-value wording with "Throws ForbiddenException if canView() returns false."
raw_findings.title: Correct the requireView Javadoc contract
raw_findings.trigger: A caller or generated API documentation consults the newly added Javadoc for requireView().

validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that getOrCreateResource doesn't set resource type is incorrect. Looking at AdminPermissionsSchema.java lines 103-110, getOrCreateResource creates resources and updates scopes but indeed doesn't call setType(). However, the init() method at lines 247-252 does set resource.setType(type) for all-resource resources. The candidate claims individual client resources lack type, but getOrCreateResource is for creating per-object resources, and the findByType query at line 138 would only find the all-clients resource anyway. The impact is speculative without proof that per-client resources should have the type set.

validated_findings.body: The administrator can manage client scopes because canManageClientScopes checks MANAGE, and can view individual client scopes because canView(ClientScopeModel) checks MANAGE, but is denied the collection-level view operation.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A principal receives Forbidden for client-scope listing despite holding the stronger management permission.
validated_findings.impact: The administrator can manage client scopes because canManageClientScopes checks MANAGE, and can view individual client scopes because canView(ClientScopeModel) checks MANAGE, but is denied the collection-level view operation.
validated_findings.root_cause: The V2 global view predicate does not preserve the manage-implies-view relationship used by the client-scope permission methods.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Include hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) in canView(), or override canViewClientScopes() to allow the all-clients MANAGE grant.
validated_findings.title: Treat an all-clients MANAGE grant as permission to view client scopes
validated_findings.trigger: An administrator has only the V2 all-clients MANAGE permission and calls an endpoint guarded by requireViewClientScopes(), such as listing realm client scopes.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about manage-implies-view inconsistency requires examining the full permission hierarchy. Line 87 shows canView() checks VIEW permission. canViewClientScopes() at ClientPermissions.java line 489-490 returns canView(). The candidate claims MANAGE should imply VIEW for client scopes, but canView() at line 87 doesn't include MANAGE check. However, canView(ClientScopeModel) at line 118-121 does check both VIEW and MANAGE. The inconsistency claim between global canView() and canViewClientScopes() is not clearly a bug - it may be intentional design.

validated_findings.body: The outer condition passes, but management() selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever V2 is enabled. The event handler then calls a V2 setPermissionsEnabled method, which throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing removal-event processing to fail.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Provider event processing aborts with UnsupportedOperationException in a valid combined-feature configuration.
validated_findings.impact: The outer condition passes, but management() selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever V2 is enabled. The event handler then calls a V2 setPermissionsEnabled method, which throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing removal-event processing to fail.
validated_findings.root_cause: The listener is gated by V1 alone even though evaluator selection gives V2 precedence.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Only run this legacy cleanup branch when V1 is enabled and V2 is disabled, or implement a V2-specific removal cleanup path that does not invoke unsupported legacy methods.
validated_findings.title: Do not dispatch removal cleanup to V2 evaluators when both feature versions are enabled
validated_findings.trigger: Both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 are enabled and a role, client, or group removal event is emitted.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch at line 77 adds a guard checking only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but management() at lines 66-70 returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when V2 is enabled. MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2 which throws UnsupportedOperationException for setPermissionsEnabled() at line 193-194. When both V1 and V2 are enabled, the V1 guard passes but V2 evaluator is used, causing the exception. This is a valid bug.

validated_findings.body: The new guard skips the ClientRemovedEvent branch entirely. The target client is deleted, but its resource and policies remain in the admin-permissions resource server as orphaned authorization data.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Deleted clients leave stale permission resources and policies in persistent authorization storage.
validated_findings.impact: The new guard skips the ClientRemovedEvent branch entirely. The target client is deleted, but its resource and policies remain in the admin-permissions resource server as orphaned authorization data.
validated_findings.root_cause: The V1-only feature guard suppresses all removal handling under the normal V2-only configuration.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add V2-specific cleanup for ClientRemovedEvent that deletes the schema resource and its associated permissions, while keeping the legacy setPermissionsEnabled cleanup confined to V1.
validated_findings.title: Remove V2 client authorization resources when their client is deleted
validated_findings.trigger: Only V2 is enabled, a client has one or more per-client V2 permission resources, and that client is deleted.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Related to candidate 5 but describes a different impact. When only V2 is enabled, Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) at line 77 returns false, so the entire cleanup block is skipped. ClientRemovedEvent handling at lines 89-91 never executes under V2-only configuration, leaving orphaned authorization resources. This is a distinct issue from candidate 5 (which is about both features enabled causing exceptions).
